controls: two graphs: every msg.value tx as an edge; funder (first ETH in) + sweep (last ETH out) as edges
strongly/weakly connected subgraphs; 'Large subgraphs are broken down using the Louvain Community Detection Algorithm'

controls: 'Real users should not be hurt; we aim to maximize precision over recall'

'Silhouette Score: Ensure high cluster validity by including only samples with a Silhouette score > 0.7'

controls: phase 1: 'Community detection algorithms like Louvain and K-Core' on asset-transfer graphs (patterns: star divergence, star convergence, tree, chain)
phase 2: K-means on transactional+profile variables; 'Addresses that are located far from the Centroid, beyond a specified threshold, are excluded from the cluster'
no numeric thresholds disclosed; zkSync NFT case: 74-account chain-like funding cluster (Medium, S)
prior_art.maps_to_sybilkit: community detection + per-member outlier removal (behavioural distance from cluster centroid)

controls: supervised subgraph LightGBM on 2-layer transaction subgraphs; 75 features: 7 time (first gas receipt, first tx, first activity, last tx, intervals), 60 amount, 8 network (degree, neighbour counts)
labels: manual analysis + 'manual appeal review process. Only addresses that did not appeal or had their appeals rejected after thorough manual review were classified as confirmed sybil addresses'
cleaning: excluded institutional addresses (hot wallets, contracts) via Arkham labels; RETAINED contract-distributed funding (disperse-style) as a sybil pattern; dropped lifecycles >1 year (2.6%)
note: 'born together act together' phrase is NOT in this paper (orchestrator paraphrase); the paper's term is 'just-in-time' temporal clustering of first-gas/first-tx/first-activity
prior_art.numbers: 193,701 addresses (23,240 sybil); Subgraph-LightGBM P=0.9428 R=0.9182 F1=0.9303 AUC=0.9806 vs Trusta clustering P=0.7962 R=0.8159; plain LightGBM P=0.7821; 'The Precision of traditional models is too low for practical requirements, leading to numerous False Positives'
prior_art.maps_to_sybilkit: appeal-validated labels; per-address (node-level) classification; 'first gas receipt -> first deposit' interval as a strong feature; do not exclude Disperse (it is a farm tool)

prior_art.program: Kaczynski & Wiacek, IJET 2026 'Airdrop Sybil Attack detection framework supported by ML' (ZKsync)
controls: phase 0: GIN topology classifier on maximal connected components of size 10-300 (ETH) / 10-900 (ZKsync); manual labels: chain >10 addresses = sybil; 'normal' needs >=0.01 ETH transfers between accounts

phase 2: DBSCAN on account-creation timestamps, eps = 14400 s (4 h), minPts = 3 — 'only two accounts created within four hours could be coincidence'; proposes multi-scale eps in {1h,4h,8h,16h,24h} with graded score
phase 3: avg gas usage < mu - sigma
score = weighted sum (0.9,0.5,0.6,0.3), threshold 0.6; 'DEX and CEX addresses should be searched and excluded'
result: 76% of 49,249 EOAs marked sybil — the paper itself warns 'filtering wallets too strictly ... may discourage beneficial, honest users'
prior_art.numbers: 37,563 of 49,249 flagged; only 342 overlap with zkSync's own eligible list
prior_art.maps_to_sybilkit: time-coincidence with minPts>=3 and eps<=4h; graded (multi-scale) temporal strength; CEX/DEX exclusion; cautionary: topology-only gets 76% FP-prone flags

prior_art.program: arXiv 2607.27370 'Compression-Based Behavioral Similarity for Open-World Sybil Discovery on Ethereum'
controls: NCD over transaction 'grammars' (rhythm/structure/intent); kNN retrieval instead of connected components; 'Blind-Spot Protocol' removes high-purity contracts (P>=0.95) that act as label shortcuts; min 10 txs per wallet
notes CEX/disperser intermediates weaken graph signals; removed ENS controller (human signal) and Uniswap router (MEV signal) as shortcuts
prior_art.numbers: 14,161 wallets (9,204 organic / 3,202 MEV / 1,755 sybil from Hop list); 1-NN acc 0.696, top-10 purity 0.754, top-10 recall 0.922
prior_art.maps_to_sybilkit: similarity retrieval with a purity cutoff rather than transitive union; gas/rhythm fingerprints as per-node similarity

controls: '~42% of labeled sybils and ~32% of ordinary wallets share a distributor-range funder (11-1000 outbound) ... statistically identical at every threshold — precision stays at the ~9% base rate ... flagged 34% of ordinary wallets'
prior_art.maps_to_sybilkit: funder fan-out is NOT a conviction signal; use it only to EXCLUDE hubs (infra), never to weld

literature.ref: Traag, Waltman, van Eck 2019 'From Louvain to Leiden' Sci Rep 9:5233
literature.point: Louvain yields up to 25% badly-connected and 16% disconnected communities; Leiden guarantees connected, well-connected communities

literature.ref: Fortunato & Barthelemy 2007 'Resolution limit in community detection' PNAS 104:36
literature.point: modularity merges small communities below a size ~sqrt(2m); needs a resolution parameter

literature.ref: Lancichinetti, Radicchi, Ramasco, Fortunato 2011 'Finding statistically significant communities in networks' PLoS ONE 6:e18961 (OSLOM)
literature.point: cluster significance vs a configuration-model null; only clusters unlikely under random fluctuations are kept

literature.ref: Cohen 2008 'Trusses: cohesive subgraphs for social network analysis' (NSA tech report)
literature.point: k-truss: every edge in >=k-2 triangles; immune to single-edge chaining
connected components first, Louvain to break large subgraphs

graph_methods.why_connected_components_over_merge_here: sybilkit emits SPANNING CHAINS (Edge docstring) so every group is a path; union-find over paths is single-linkage clustering — one weak edge anywhere merges two groups, and there is no notion of density. Measured on the live tier-A graph restricted to the 11,573 flagged nodes: 4,157 bridges and 4,168 articulation points (degree histogram 1:385, 2:4,436, 3:2,132, 4+:4,620); bridge edge kinds: round-wave 2,647, split 2,448, drip 1,102, exact-odd 674, sequence 613, near-block 67, burst 49; 1,954 bridges carry ONLY weak kinds; cutting them leaves 9,692 members in components >=5 and drops 1,881 below min_size.

policy_simulation_on_this_dataset.note: same edge set as the live run; STRONG={amount:exact_odd, sequence, cadence:burst, cadence:drip, funding:peel_chain}; WEAK={round_wave, split, near_same_block, shared_hub, gas}. controls = the 60 benchmark controls (weakly labeled); farm_windows = the 11 audited operator waves (recall).

policies.policy: P3 per-node: member touches >=1 strong-rule edge
P4 per-node: >=2 families at the node AND >=1 strong
P4b per-node: >=2 families at the node (any)
P5 strong-edge-only components, min_size 5 (families not gated)
P5b strong-edge-only components, min_size 5, >=2 strong families
P5 strong-edge-only components, min_size 10 (families not gated)
P5b strong-edge-only components, min_size 10, >=2 strong families
P5 strong-edge-only components, min_size 20 (families not gated)
P5b strong-edge-only components, min_size 20, >=2 strong families
P6 infra = 12 CEX + first-funders with fan-out >= 20 (25 funders)
P6 infra = 12 CEX + first-funders with fan-out >= 50 (13 funders)
P6b infra = 12 CEX + Disperse contract only
P6c shared-hub rule removed (peel chain kept)
P7 combined: fan-out>=20 infra + min_size 10 + per-node >=1 strong
P7b combined: fan-out>=20 infra + min_size 10 + per-node >=2 families incl. strong
P8 cluster needs >=50% strong-touching members; keep only those members

null_model_reference.point: on a synthetic operator-free population (14,262 wallets, human amount prior from ENS singles, 40% CEX-funded) the SHIPPED rules flag 6,382 wallets (44.7%) across 41 clusters — dominated by amount+funding (110) and cadence+sequence (76) combos; the strictest candidate variant flags 14.6 (0.1%)

cheap_onchain_infra_heuristics.this_dataset: 6 exchange-scale first funders: 1.7M-9.9M txs, up to 18,330 ETH (agent_xhub.json labels: Bitget 6, Binance 18, OKX Hot Wallet 3, FTX 2 (stale), OKX 24, OKX 3); farm distributors are tiny by comparison (0x3c15… 5,725 txs; 0x2fc9… 38 txs). cheap_onchain_infra_heuristics.thresholds_used_elsewhere: Chaos Labs: label-based (CEX/DEX/bridge) + first native transfer; Arbitrum: label-based entity removal; ijet: 'DEX and CEX addresses should be searched and excluded'; 2505.09313: excluded hot wallets + contracts via labels, kept contract-distributed funding; ChainCred: fan-out 11-1000 has no discriminative power
